answer: Extracted scientific evidence from 'Exploring the impacts of climate change and identifying potential adaptation strategies for sustainable rice production in Thailand’s Lower Chao Phraya Basin through crop simulation modeling' (Vilavan et al., 2024, Environ Monit Assess 196:1192).

paper_metadata.title: Exploring the impacts of climate change and identifying potential adaptation strategies for sustainable rice production in Thailand’s Lower Chao Phraya Basin through crop simulation modeling
author_affiliations: Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), Pathum Thani, Thailand
National Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (BIOTEC), NSTDA, Pathum Thani, Thailand

study_location.region: Lower Chao Phraya River Basin (CPRB), Pathum Thani Province, Thailand
study_location.representative_site: Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) Agricultural Research Farm

section_1_crop_model_and_experimental_se.baseline_weather_period: 2010–2022 (AIT onsite weather station; missing data supplemented from Mueang, Pathum Thani station)

section_3_physiological_mechanisms.temperature_trends: Daily Tmax and Tmin increase by ~2°C under SSP2-4.5 and ~4°C under SSP5-8.5 in the late century, with peak Tmax exceeding 40°C in April.
section_3_physiological_mechanisms.day_vs_night_temperature_impacts: Both daytime Tmax and nighttime Tmin show sustained upward trends. Tmax increases noticeably from February to June (peaking in April), accelerating phenological growth while reducing biomass accumulation due to elevated maintenance respiration.
section_3_physiological_mechanisms.pollen_and_spikelet_sterility: Heat stress during panicle initiation, booting, and flowering stages impairs photosynthetic capacity and inhibits swelling of pollen grains and thecae dehiscence, causing high pollen sterility and poor grain set.
section_3_physiological_mechanisms.grain_filling_curtailment: Exposure to high temperatures shortens the grain-filling period (P5), restricting photosynthate accumulation in grains and driving up crop evapotranspiration and irrigation water demand.

planting_date_shift.early_shift_1_2_weeks: Shifting planting date 1–2 weeks earlier (to 13 July or 6 July) improves yield and reduces irrigation water demand.
planting_date_shift.late_shift_1_2_weeks: Shifting planting date 1–2 weeks later (to 27 July or 3 August) negatively impacts yield and increases water use across all scenarios.

fertilizer_management.baseline_schedule: 60 kg P/ha and 49 kg N/ha on 20 July (planting); 25 kg N/ha on 20 September (panicle initiation)
fertilizer_management.timing_shift: Shifting panicle initiation fertilizer application 1–2 weeks earlier (to 13 September or 6 September) increases yield by at least 5.6% to 6.6% under SSP5-8.5 without increasing water input.

dosage_optimization.standard_plus_50pct_1.5x: N: 112.5 kg/ha, P: 90 kg/ha. Substantially increases yield across all scenarios with negligible water demand increase.
dosage_optimization.higher_doses_2.0x_to_4.0x: Yield plateaus at 1.5x due to genetic potential limits.

irrigation_threshold_optimization.threshold_45pct: Saves ~30% irrigation water while maintaining yield stability.
irrigation_threshold_optimization.threshold_40pct: Saves ~55% irrigation water while maintaining yield stability.
irrigation_threshold_optimization.threshold_30pct: Saves up to 90% irrigation water while maintaining yield stability.

heat_tolerance_trait_THOT.impact: Increasing THOT by 5%–15% (to 32°C–36°C) delivers the largest single yield gain, up to +37.9% under SSP5-8.5 in the late century.

high_yield_potential_G1.impact: Increasing G1 by 15% (to 74) increases grain yield by +8.3% under SSP5-8.5 late century (yielding 3.46 t/ha vs. 3.19 t/ha baseline).

grain_filling_extension_P5.parameter: P5 (grain filling duration in GDD, baseline 720.4 GDD)
grain_filling_extension_P5.impact: Extending P5 by 15% (to 828.5 GDD) increases late-century SSP5-8.5 yield by +1.1% (yielding 3.23 t/ha), but involves trade-offs of increased seasonal irrigation water demand.

early_flowering_trade_offs_P1.parameter: P1 (basic vegetative phase GDD, baseline 310 GDD)
early_flowering_trade_offs_P1.impact: Decreasing P1 (265–295 GDD) reduces irrigation water demand slightly but causes yield losses due to insufficient vegetative biomass accumulation. Increasing P1 by 10% (340 GDD) yields no significant gain.

drought_tolerance_RWUMX.parameter: RWUMX (maximum root water uptake per unit root length)
drought_tolerance_RWUMX.impact: Under fully irrigated basin conditions, adjusting RWUMX shows negligible impact on overall yield or water savings.

policy_recommendations_for_DCCE_and_NAP: Integrate Genotype-by-Management (G×M) package recommendations into Thailand's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) for agriculture.
Prioritize genetic breeding programs for heat-tolerant cultivars (enhancing the THOT trait) to insulate rice against extreme warming beyond mid-century.

Promote low-cost agronomic adjustments: advance planting by 1–2 weeks (early July), advance panicle initiation N application by 1–2 weeks (early September), and adjust N rate to 1.5x recommended dose (112.5 kg N/ha).
Institutionalize Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation guidelines by lowering soil moisture thresholds to 30%–40%, capturing 55%–90% irrigation water savings while maintaining yield.
Strengthen local extension networks to overcome cultural inertia and facilitate farmer adoption of shifted planting and irrigation schedules.
